  unfair to CUBIC on shared
  bottlenecks, a problem the
  BBRv2/v3 line explicitly
  targets.


  The latest shift is where
  the algorithm lives. QUIC
  implements congestion
  control in userspace, so
  improvements ship with
  applications instead of
  waiting on kernel releases.
   Specialized regimes have
  their own controllers —
  DCQCN for RDMA datacenters,
   Swift and Copa for tail
  latency, tuned profiles for
   5G.

  Four decades on, the
  skeleton is unchanged:
  probe gently, back off
  multiplicatively, share
  fairly. What evolved is
  everything around that
  skeleton — what counts as
  congestion evidence, how
  fast capacity is probed,
  and where the algorithm
  runs.

  DONE

✻ Worked for 6s
